_comment: Custom product page plan. Each page is a separate, reviewable App Store product page with its own URL, screenshots and search keyword set, reachable only from a link you control — an ad, a creator video, a landing page. The point of a CPP is that it captures a search term or a promise the main page does not win, so the keyword sets here are deliberately disjoint from the single words already in store/asc/listings.json (which owns fashion, closet, organizer, virtual, headshot, capsule, planner, ootd and their translations). Consumed by: node scripts/asc/grow.mjs cpp. Also readable by node scripts/asc/publish.mjs cpp, which uses only name/locales/promotionalText.
_templateComment: The product page template a new CPP copies its layout and inherited screenshots from. Must be a version that is READY_FOR_SALE or in PREPARE_FOR_SUBMISSION. grow.mjs resolves this at run time and refuses to guess.
_localeComment: Seven locales with hand-written promotional copy, not machine output. A CPP localized with English fallback text shows a foreign-language promise to a user who searched in their own language, which converts worse than the main page it replaced. Grow this list when the copy is written, not before.

frameSemantics.1: closet  - wardrobe grid, the whole closet as searchable data
frameSemantics.2: daily   - home screen, today's outfit from live weather
frameSemantics.3: tryon   - the outfit rendered on your own body
frameSemantics.4: photoshoot - studio photos from your selfies
frameSemantics.5: wear    - cost per wear, what you actually use
frameSemantics.6: offer   - one month of Pro free, then free forever

_frameComment: Frame ids and order come from store/creative/copy.json, which the render pipeline reads. That file defines six frames, not ten: Apple accepts up to ten screenshots, and the pipeline does not produce four of them yet. Every page below is written against the six that exist, and grow.mjs resolves each id against store/creative/manifest.json, refusing to place a frame that was never rendered. The rule each page follows: the LEAD frame must depict the promise in the page's name. A virtual-try-on page whose first screenshot is a wardrobe grid pays for the click and loses the install.
